beats.narration_text: You run a probe on your model and write down what you expected afterward. That's not a prediction — it's a reconstruction. The gap between what you predicted and what happened is where the learning lives. Leave the prediction editable and the gap collapses to zero: you learn nothing and the grade knows it. A SHA-256 hash and thirty lines of Python take the edit away.

props.command: a prediction you can edit after the result is worth nothing — hash it first

beats.narration_text: In the terminal: ask Claude to write a Python CLI called predlock with two subcommands. Lock takes a text string, appends the UTC timestamp, the text, and its SHA-256 hash as a JSON line to predlock.log, and prints the hash. Resolve takes a hash prefix and an outcome text, finds the locked prediction by hash, appends the outcome, and prints prediction and outcome side by side plus 'HASH VERIFIED' if the stored text still hashes to the given hash.

props.command:
claude "Write a Python CLI 'predlock' with two subcommands:
(1) 'lock <text>' — append
    {utc_timestamp, text, sha256(text)}
    as JSON line to predlock.log, print the hash
(2) 'resolve <hash> <outcome_text>' — find locked
    prediction by hash, append outcome, print
    prediction vs outcome + HASH VERIFIED or MISMATCH"

beats.role_note: terminal (Onda) — read the output before running
beats.narration_text: Read the two functions before running. Lock does three things: compute SHA-256 of the text, build a JSON record with the timestamp, and append it to the log — one line, append-only, never overwritten. Resolve does one verification: it reads the stored text back from the log and hashes it again. If the hash still matches, the prediction was not edited. If it doesn't, it was. The tamper-evidence is not cryptographic; it's structural. The log is the audit trail.

props.title: predlock.py
props.code:
# predlock.py — Claude Code output
import hashlib, json, datetime
from pathlib import Path

LOG = Path("predlock.log")

def lock(text: str) -> str:
    h = hashlib.sha256(text.encode()).hexdigest()
    record = {
        "utc": datetime.datetime.utcnow().isoformat(),
        "text": text,
        "sha256": h,
    }
    with LOG.open("a") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps(record) + "\n")
    return h  # print this; you can't re-derive it later

def resolve(hash_prefix: str, outcome: str):
    for line in LOG.read_text().splitlines():
        r = json.loads(line)
        if r["sha256"].startswith(hash_prefix):
            verified = (
                hashlib.sha256(r["text"].encode()).hexdigest()
                == r["sha256"]
            )
            print(f"PREDICTION: {r['text']}")
            print(f"OUTCOME:    {outcome}")
            print("HASH VERIFIED" if verified else "HASH MISMATCH")

beats.role_note: screen-recording — lock before probe, resolve after, then tamper test
beats.narration_text: Lock a prediction before running the probe: 'I expect ECE on the shifted slice to be under point-one.' Hash prints. Run the probe — ECE comes back at point-nineteen. Resolve with the hash: prediction prints, outcome prints, HASH VERIFIED. The gap is visible and real. Now edit the locked line in the log — change 'under point-one' to 'around point-two' — and resolve again. HASH MISMATCH. The edit is detectable.
beats.visual_intent: screen-recording: predlock lock (hash prints) → probe runs (ECE=0.19) → predlock resolve (HASH VERIFIED, gap visible) → log edited manually → predlock resolve again (HASH MISMATCH)

props.title: terminal: predlock demo
props.code:
$ python predlock.py lock "ECE on shifted slice < 0.10"
Hash: a3f7c2d1

[...probe runs, ECE = 0.19...]

$ python predlock.py resolve a3f7c2d1 "ECE = 0.19"
PREDICTION: ECE on shifted slice < 0.10
OUTCOME:    ECE = 0.19
HASH VERIFIED

[...manually edit log line...]

$ python predlock.py resolve a3f7c2d1 "ECE = 0.19"
HASH MISMATCH  ← edit detected

beats.role_note: terminal (Onda) — wire as pre-step to any instrument script
beats.narration_text: Wire the lock as the first line of any instrument script so no probe runs without a locked prediction. Ask Claude to add a --require flag: if predlock.log has no locked entry in the last twenty-four hours, exit with code one and print 'No prediction locked — run predlock lock first.' Then show a bash wrapper that enforces it before every probe runs.

props.command:
claude "Update predlock.py: add --require flag.
If predlock.log has no entry in last 24 hours,
exit code 1: 'No prediction locked. Run: predlock lock'
Add a bash wrapper run_probe.sh that runs
  python predlock.py --require &&
  python $1
so no probe script runs without a locked prediction."

beats.narration_text: The information in an audit lives in the gap between prediction and outcome. Leave the prediction editable and the gap collapses to zero — you learn nothing and the grade knows it. The lock is thirty lines of Python and a SHA-256 hash. Wire it as the first step in every probe and it stops being a rule you might forget and becomes a step you can't skip. A surprise you predicted against beats a confirmation you assumed — and you can only know which one you got if the prediction was locked before you looked.

beats.narration_text: Your move: before you run any other candidate's instrument script — calibration curve, distribution shift, confusion matrix — run predlock lock with your expected finding first. Then resolve it after. The gap between what you guessed and what you got is the only number that measures your model intuition, and you can only measure it if you can't change it.
